title: Lesson 36: Sharing Architecture Deep Dive: Recalculation, Implicit Sharing, and When Sharing Can't Do the Job
description: Sharing as a live and bounded mechanism: the cost of recalculation, implicit sharing the platform grants without asking, and the tools that take over when declarative sharing cannot do the job.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Sharing Architecture Deep Dive: Recalculation, Implicit Sharing, and When Sharing Can't Do the Job”, an architect changes a high-volume object’s org-wide default from Private to Read Only on a large org. What runs in the background?
options: Nothing; the flag flips and existing share records are left exactly as they were.
A one-time Apex managed sharing recalculation class, which the architect has to write and associate with the object.
A sharing recalculation that walks existing records and updates share records, and it may also delete shares that now grant no additional access.
A role hierarchy rebuild, because roles determine the default access level for an object.
questions.explanation: A recalculation is a cleanup pass as well as an expansion, so on a large object it is a scheduled event with a maintenance window rather than an impulse change.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: If a user can see a child opportunity, case, contact, or order, they implicitly see the associated account, and the account hierarchy does not roll access up the way the role hierarchy does.
Implicit sharing applies to custom objects as well as standard parent-child pairings, and it can be disabled per object.
The account hierarchy rolls access up from a child account to its parent, exactly like the role hierarchy.
Implicit sharing is a configurable setting that an administrator turns on when parent access should follow child access.
questions.explanation: Implicit sharing is native and cannot be turned on or off, it only covers those standard parent-child pairings, and the account hierarchy is not a sharing relationship as the role hierarchy is.

questions.question: Which conclusion does the lesson support?
options: When certain users see too much, an additional sharing rule narrows their access back down.

Restriction rules are the declarative mechanism that narrows access, while Apex managed sharing is the escalation for requirements no declarative method can express, carrying a RowCause from a defined sharing reason.
A manual share survives a record owner change, which is why it is the right tool when an external system of truth drives access.
Apex managed sharing bypasses the sharing model and is recalculated separately from the rest of the org’s shares.
questions.explanation: Sharing rules and manual shares only ever open access, so genuinely private access is a restriction rule, and dynamic access that survives an owner transfer is Apex managed sharing.
